def test_minSubArraySum():
    # All positive numbers -> minimum is the smallest element
    assert minSubArraySum([2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 4]) == 1
    assert minSubArraySum([1, 2, 3]) == 1
    assert minSubArraySum([10, 20, 30, 40, 100, 90, 80, 70]) == 10
    assert minSubArraySum([100, 1, 457, 9, 1, 87, 24, 7, 8, 19, 19, 40]) == 1

    # All negative numbers -> minimum is the sum of the whole array
    assert minSubArraySum([-1, -2, -3]) == -6
    assert minSubArraySum([-1, -2, -3, -4]) == -10

    # Single element arrays
    assert minSubArraySum([0]) == 0
    assert minSubArraySum([-1]) == -1
    assert minSubArraySum([5]) == 5

    # Arrays containing zero
    assert minSubArraySum([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) == 0
    assert minSubArraySum([1, 0, -2]) == -2

    # Mixed positive and negative numbers
    assert minSubArraySum([1, -1]) == -1
    assert minSubArraySum([3, -4, 1, -1]) == -4
    assert minSubArraySum([1, -2, 3, -5, 4]) == -5
    assert minSubArraySum([5, -3, 2, -1]) == -3
    assert minSubArraySum([-1, 2, -3]) == -3
    assert minSubArraySum([2, -3, 4, -1, 2]) == -3

    # Larger mixed array
    assert minSubArraySum([1, -2, -3, 4, -5, 6]) == -5

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_minSubArraySum()
